subject: humanities
passage: Gothic cathedrals such as Chartres owe their soaring, light-filled interiors to an engineering device: the flying buttress. These external arches carry the outward thrust of a high stone vault across open air to massive piers set away from the building. With the walls relieved of much of that load, builders could make them thinner and fill them with large expanses of stained glass. The buttress, in this view, is a structural solution and nothing more.
passage_b: No one doubts that flying buttresses did essential structural work; without them, the great windows of Gothic churches could not have stood. Yet medieval masons did not leave them plain. They carved the arches with tracery, set statues in niches along the piers, and added ornament that served no structural purpose. To treat the buttress purely as engineering is to ignore how deliberately its builders made it part of the building's display.
stem: Based on the texts, both authors would most likely agree with which statement?

choices.A: Flying buttresses were first built as decoration and only later took on structural work.
choices.B: Medieval masons regarded flying buttresses as purely structural devices.
choices.C: The carving on flying buttresses was added to help them resist the thrust of the vault.
choices.D: Flying buttresses made it possible for builders to use larger windows.

explanation.why: Text 1 says that with buttresses carrying the vault's thrust, builders could "fill [the walls] with large expanses of stained glass." Text 2 agrees that "without them, the great windows of Gothic churches could not have stood." Both authors therefore accept that buttresses allowed larger windows; they disagree only about whether the buttress was also display.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Neither text says buttresses began as decoration; both treat their structural work as essential.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 1 presents the buttress as purely structural, but Text 2 argues that masons deliberately made it part of the display.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 says the ornament "served no structural purpose," so it would reject this.
explanation.D: Correct. Both texts say buttresses let builders open the walls for great windows of stained glass.
